references.text: On the tenth day of the first month, the Passover lamb was chosen, on the same date that the Israelites crossed the Jordan and camped at Gilgal.
The Israelites left Egypt in the first month, linking the time of their departure to the crossing of the Jordan.
Gilgal is mentioned as the place where the Israelites celebrated Passover after crossing the Jordan, and where the disgrace of Egypt was rolled away.
At Gilgal, the Israelites were circumcised before celebrating Passover, in connection with their arrival on the tenth day of the first month.
Gilgal was an important place in Israel's history, where Samuel judged the people on a regular circuit.
Gilgal was the place where Saul was confirmed as king, an important gathering place for Israel.
The prophet Micah refers to the events from Shittim to Gilgal as a testimony of the Lord's righteous acts.
